**[SUGGESTION]:** 60-second stall ceiling is shorter than the deadline bound the stall primitive exists to exercise

`ghdeadline` accepts `GH_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` up to 5m and defaults to 5m when unset (scripts/ghdeadline/main.go:16-24). For any deadline above 60s this "stalled" child wakes, returns, and exits 0 - the gh call then *succeeds* with empty output and the deadline bound is never exercised. The only current consumer pins 100ms (scripts/test/test_homebrew.sh:45), so nothing fails today, but the primitive is silently coupled to sub-minute deadlines: a future deadline control using the default five-minute bound would fail later with an unrelated diagnostic (e.g. the `jq -e` tap assertion) instead of `GitHub deadline: ...`. Consider sleeping past the 5m ceiling or deriving the stall from the configured deadline.

---
Reply with `@kilocode-bot fix it` to have Kilo Code address this issue.

**[SUGGESTION]:** New `check()` helper and signal sub-test sit outside every shellcheck target

`lint-release-promotion` shellchecks the promote/metadata/candidate/homebrew scripts and their test suites (exactly those eight files, confirmed in the retained lint.log), but `test_gh_fixture.sh` - which this commit extends with a function, shifted-argument handling and a conditional sub-test - is only executed via `test-gh-fixture`, never linted. The three sibling suites that received the same launcher wiring all live under the lint gate; adding this file to the shellcheck list would keep the new helper covered by the same static analysis.

---
Reply with `@kilocode-bot fix it` to have Kilo Code address this issue.

**[SUGGESTION]:** Base `invoke` omits the hostile-env trio the sibling launcher suites bake in

test_candidate.sh:101, test_promotion.sh:141 and test_metadata.sh:75 all include `GH_HOST=wrong.example GH_DEBUG=api DEBUG=1` in their base env arrays, so every fixture invocation challenges the script's environment sanitization; here the trio is attached only to the happy-path tap check (line 44), leaving the missing-tap and deadline invocations running with the ambient environment. homebrew.sh:6-7 currently overrides/unsets those vars unconditionally, so this is convention divergence rather than a live hole - but a future homebrew.sh change that sanitizes conditionally would pass this suite unchallenged on two of its three invocation paths.

---
Reply with `@kilocode-bot fix it` to have Kilo Code address this issue.

**[SUGGESTION]:** Probe validates the PATH jq while the wrapper requires an undocumented `MODEL_REAL_JQ`

The retained wrapper invokes `"$MODEL_REAL_JQ" --binary "$@"` exclusively (bin/jq:10 - no PATH fallback; unset fails under `set -u` with an unbound-variable error), and the sanctioned replay script binds it from `command -v jq` (r10-jq-crlf-model.sh:4-6). This README, whose stated purpose (R11-05) is recording the model's previously unstated tool prerequisites, never mentions `MODEL_REAL_JQ`: a replayer following it literally hits an unexplained unbound-variable failure, and the suggested probe `jq --binary --null-input empty` can validate a different binary than the one the wrapper will actually execute. Document the mandatory selector alongside the capability note, and probe `$MODEL_REAL_JQ --binary --null-input empty` instead of the PATH jq.

---
Reply with `@kilocode-bot fix it` to have Kilo Code address this issue.

**[SUGGESTION]:** Cross-build logs cannot evidence which platform they built for

This log and cross-fixture-darwin.log are byte-identical single lines - the make-echoed recipe - with no `GOOS`/`GOARCH`, no compiler identity and no success marker. The windows/amd64 and darwin/amd64 attributions in acceptance.json's `cross_builds` therefore rest solely on the receipt's own `exit: 0` fields and cannot be audited from the retained logs, unlike the rest of this repo's evidence discipline. Recording `go env GOOS GOARCH` (or the exact `GOOS=... make build-gh-fixture` invocation) alongside each build would make these receipts self-proving.

---
Reply with `@kilocode-bot fix it` to have Kilo Code address this issue.
